narr: A series of thunderstorms brought torrential rainfall and widespread flooding to much of the Chicago metro area, namely the south and west suburbs and up into the city of Chicago. Several Oswego District 308 schools received water and storm damage. Flood damages were estimated at around $288 million across the metro area, most of which came from the city of Chicago which alone accounted for roughly $230 million in damages with roughly 40,000 individual structures flooded around the city. The remainder of Cook County accounted for roughly $57 million in flood damages with more than 10,000 additional structures flooded. Several instances of wind damage were also reported, mostly damage to trees.
ev: An estimated 20 structures were flooded in southern Kane County, specifically in the Aurora and Montgomery areas, amounting to roughly $15,000 in damages.

Significant flooding was reported around parts of northern Will County, namely in the vicinities of Joliet, Romeoville, and Plainfield. In Joliet, Caton Farm Rd was closed at Joe Adler Dr, and IL Rt. 53 was closed at a viaduct south of Caton Farm Rd due to flooding. A car was reported stranded in floodwater near Center St north of I-80 in Joliet. In Crest Hill, street flooding was reported at IL Rt. 53 and Theodore St. Standing water was reported at IL-126 and County Line Rd in Plainfield. An estimated 250 structures were flooded in this area amounting to around $1 million in flood damages.
Interstate 55 was closed in both directions at Pulaski Rd due to flooding.
Multiple reports of flooded basements came out of Chicago's Greater Grand Crossing community area.
Two feet of standing water was reported in yards and on sidewalks in Wood Dale.

Significant basement flooding was reported in Boulder Hill. A car was also reported floating in floodwater. One private weather station in town recorded 5.1 of 24-hour rainfall on the morning of the 17th, and another recorded 4.5.
Three to four feet of standing water were reported in Oswego's Fox Chase subdivision.

Widespread flash flooding impacted the southwest side of Chicago. The city received over 3,000 service requests for water in basements, a large majority of which were from areas near and east of Midway Airport. The highest concentration of reports were out of the West Lawn, Chicago Lawn, Marquette Park, and Gage Park community areas. A photo shared via social media showed at least six inches of standing water on roads and sidewalks in Gage Park. Near W 47th St and Archer Ave, at least four cars were stranded in a flooded viaduct. Another viaduct was flooded at 75th St and S Western Ave in Beverly View. By the morning of the 17th, 24-hour rainfall reports from around the area ranged between two and three inches.

At Oswego High School, prolonged intense rainfall overwhelmed the capacity of a storm drainage system. Up to two feet of water flooded a courtyard near the school. Water flowed from the courtyard into the school via a set of double doors and reached depths of 8 to 10 inches near the entrance to the building. Water proceeded to flow into hallways, athletic facilities, and the gymnasium. The damage required the gym floor to be replaced. Damages amounted to over $300,000, with the gym floor alone costing around $250,000.

Roughly 40,000 structures sustained flood damage around the city of Chicago. The greatest impacts were felt across the southwest side near and east of Midway Airport, but reports came in from all across the city. Chicago alone accounted for approximately $230 million in flood damages.
Approximately 500 structures were flooded in Chicago's west suburbs, including Northlake and Maywood, totaling about $2 million in damages.
Flood damages were estimated at $55 million as around 10,000 structures flooded across Chicago's near southwest suburbs, including Riverside, Berwyn, Cicero, and Summit.
North Paulina St was flooded in the Rogers Park neighborhood of Chicago.
At least two cars were stuck in floodwaters underneath a viaduct at E 95th St and S Cottage Grove Ave in Cottage Grove Heights. At least one was towed out.
